content.rule: All operational instructions, task-control prompts, glossary entries, and examples in this JSONL are written in English.
content.reason: Coding agents generally follow technical instructions more reliably when the prompt uses precise English terminology.
content.exception: Repository file names, command names, code symbols, and user-provided identifiers must remain exact.

truth: SnapSurf-lang is a foundation-stage systems language project for Linux x86_64.
The active root compiler path is FASM/CMake.
Root CMake builds build/surf from compiler/fasm/main.asm.
The foundation compiler is not complete.
The full language design is not complete.
engineering_direction: Keep the active compiler implementation FASM-first.
Move toward a fast, correct, low-level systems language compiler.
Prefer explicit low-level data structures and audited assembly routines over speculative abstractions.
Correctness comes before performance; performance work requires measurement.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim SnapSurf is self-hosting.
Do not claim the foundation compiler is complete.
Do not claim the language design is complete.
Do not claim completion without command evidence.

content.decision: Do not put the user's sudo password into prompts, context.jsonl, repository files, scripts, or any AI-readable file.
reason: Long-running agents can hallucinate, leak, paste, log, or misuse secrets.
A sudo password in context becomes unsafe ambient authority.
Normal SnapSurf repository coding, building, and testing should not require root access.
allowed_without_asking: Editing project files required by the task.
sudo_rule: Do not run sudo during repository coding tasks.
If a dependency is missing, first confirm with command -v.
If root installation is truly required, record a blocker in context.jsonl and ask the user to install it manually.
Never request, store, echo, or infer the sudo password.
Never change OS, package manager, bootloader, disk, SELinux, firewall, or security settings while working on SnapSurf source.

content.truth: A prompt cannot turn a model into real AGI.
content.allowed_target: Force AGI-like engineering rigor: persistent state, whole-repository grounding, adversarial self-review, proof-based completion, and strict failure recovery.
content.objective: Make the agent behave as close as possible to a careful senior systems engineer working under long-run degradation risk.
do_not_claim: Do not claim to be AGI.
Do not claim completion without proof.
agi_like_standard: Never rely on memory when project state can be read from disk.
Never trust a conclusion without a check.
Never trust one check when the work affects compiler correctness.
Never proceed after a mismatch between code, plan, tests, and the original objective.
Always prefer verified repository facts over assumptions.

content.purpose: Convert known failure modes into hard operating rules.

failures_and_rules.failure: Local Codex goal history was lost after OS reinstall because ~/.codex was not backed up.
failures_and_rules.rule: Always create durable context.jsonl inside the repository. Backup ~/.codex and VS Code state outside the repo before OS changes.

failures_and_rules.failure: Long tasks cause hallucination, spec drift, and shallow completion.
failures_and_rules.rule: Use context.jsonl as a state machine. Every phase starts by reading it and ends by updating it.

failures_and_rules.failure: Agent may split long work into phases and stop after partial progress.
failures_and_rules.rule: Phases are execution chunks only, never scope reduction. Continue until final_done_condition or blocker.

failures_and_rules.failure: Agent may say complete after smoke tests.
failures_and_rules.rule: Smoke and discovery gates are narrow gates only. Full regression is required for final completion when compiler behavior changes.

failures_and_rules.failure: Agent may code after reading only one file or one grep result.
failures_and_rules.rule: Whole-project analysis is mandatory before source edits.

failures_and_rules.failure: Agent may follow stale NASM-era docs or old reference implementation.
failures_and_rules.rule: Active path is FASM/CMake. compiler/asm and prototypes/rust_stage0 are reference-only.
Minimum surgical implementation only. Every changed line must trace to user objective, test, or required compiler fix.

failures_and_rules.failure: Agent may create report Markdown instead of doing implementation.
failures_and_rules.rule: No new Markdown report files. Only context.jsonl for state, plus source/test files required by the task.

failures_and_rules.failure: Agent may ask for sudo/password or run risky system commands.
failures_and_rules.rule: No sudo. No password. Missing tools become blockers for the user to handle manually.

failures_and_rules.failure: Agent may edit multiple files before verifying the first one.
failures_and_rules.rule: After each edited file, four passed checks are mandatory before editing the next source file.

failures_and_rules.failure: Agent may optimize without baseline and regress performance.
failures_and_rules.rule: Performance-sensitive work requires before/after baseline. A measured regression of 1% or more fails unless explicitly justified by correctness, security, or stability.

failures_and_rules.failure: Agent may silently reinterpret an incomplete prompt.
failures_and_rules.rule: If the spec is incomplete but direction is clear, use the hardcore FASM-first fallback and record rejected alternatives.
Uncertainty must be recorded as an assumption, ambiguity, fallback decision, or blocker.

content.purpose: Define key terms so the coding agent cannot reinterpret them loosely.

terms.definition: A line-delimited JSON execution log inside the repository. It is the agent's durable task memory.
terms.example: {"type":"phase_start","phase_id":"P2","objective":"audit parser_expr.asm before editing"}

terms.definition: A controlled workflow where each next action depends on the last recorded state.
terms.example: If context.jsonl shows P3 incomplete, resume P3 instead of starting a new plan.

terms.definition: Reading enough of the repository to understand architecture, active build path, tests, invariants, and risks before editing.
terms.example: Read README.md, memory/*.md, CMakeLists.txt, compiler/fasm/main.asm include graph, docs, tests, examples, and relevant modules before changing parser_expr.asm.

terms.definition: The code path currently used by the root build and runtime behavior.
terms.example: compiler/fasm/main.asm is active because CMake builds build/surf from it.

terms.definition: Code kept for comparison or historical guidance but not used by the active root build.
terms.example: compiler/asm and prototypes/rust_stage0 may be read for reference, but must not become active dependencies.

terms.definition: A rule that must remain true after the task.
terms.example: The root build must remain CMake + FASM, and must not call NASM.

terms.definition: The step where the agent records the objective, requirements, forbidden actions, assumptions, and final_done_condition before coding.
terms.example: Before editing, record that the task is to improve active FASM compiler correctness, not to create Markdown reports.

terms.definition: A concrete, verifiable definition of completion.
terms.example: full-regression passes, every edited file has four passed checks, and the final diff matches the original objective.

terms.definition: A bounded execution chunk with an objective, files, success criteria, and verification gate.
terms.example: P1: audit lexer; P2: edit lexer; P3: run lexer tests and full regression.

terms.definition: Reducing the user's real objective to an easier partial task without permission.
terms.example: User asks to improve compiler behavior, but the agent only writes a planning note and stops.

terms.definition: A real condition that prevents progress without user action.
terms.example: fasm is not installed. Record exact missing command and ask user to install it manually.

terms.definition: The smallest safe code change that directly satisfies the task.
terms.example: Fix one parser branch and expected test, without reformatting unrelated parser code.

terms.definition: Functionality not requested and not required to satisfy the objective.
terms.example: Adding a package registry while the task only asks to fix expression parsing.

terms.definition: A small, narrow test that checks basic operation but does not prove the full project is correct.
terms.example: cmake --build build/cmake --target fasm-smoke.

terms.definition: A command or test suite used to prove that existing behavior has not been broken.
terms.example: cmake --build build/cmake --target full-regression.

terms.definition: The strongest normal verification gate for SnapSurf's current foundation suite.
terms.example: After compiler behavior changes, run cmake --build build/cmake --target full-regression.

terms.definition: The mandatory per-file verification sequence required after editing one file.
terms.example: PASS_1 reread+diff, PASS_2 project cross-check, PASS_3 plan alignment, PASS_4 local verification.

terms.definition: Checking whether an edited file still fits callers, callees, include graph, tests, and active path.
terms.example: After changing semantic_expr.asm, search affected symbols and inspect semantic.asm callers.

terms.definition: Comparing the current change against the original objective and edit_plan.
terms.example: If the plan says fix diagnostics, do not add an optimizer.

terms.definition: The active compiler implementation and generated program path should prioritize Flat Assembler/FASM, not NASM, Rust, C, Python, or Node.
terms.example: Generated build/main.asm must be FASM syntax and build/hello must be assembled directly by FASM.

terms.definition: Completion based on files changed, command results, and recorded verification, not prose claims.
terms.example: Final status includes git diff summary, full-regression exit code, and remaining limitations.

terms.definition: A claim or decision not grounded in repository files, command output, or explicit user requirements.
terms.example: Saying SnapSurf is self-hosting even though README says it is not.

terms.definition: The procedure for continuing after interruption by reading context.jsonl and resuming the last incomplete phase/pass.
terms.example: If PASS_3 failed before interruption, resume at PASS_3, not at a new implementation.

terms.definition: The rule used when the prompt lacks full spec but the project direction is clear.
terms.example: Choose the hardest correctness-preserving FASM-first improvement and record rejected alternatives.

terms.definition: A mandatory check before appending to context.jsonl to confirm the agent still has enough reliable state to write a factual record.
terms.example: Before writing verification_result, confirm the exact command, exit code, and meaning are known.

terms.definition: A logging style where new records are appended and old records are not silently rewritten.
terms.example: If a previous assumption was wrong, append a correction record instead of editing the old line.

terms.definition: The process of reconstructing task state after interruption or memory loss by reading context.jsonl, git status, and git diff.
terms.example: After resume, read the last 80 context.jsonl records and continue from the last incomplete four-pass check.

terms.definition: Task state stored on disk rather than only in the model's temporary context window.
terms.example: context.jsonl records original objective, current phase, edited files, verification results, and next action.

content.purpose: Simulate AGI-like project control through explicit roles inside the workflow.

layers.job: Protect original_user_objective, explicit requirements, forbidden actions, and final_done_condition.
Map actual files, active path, test matrix, include graph, and reference-only zones.
Prevent Makefile, NASM, Rust prototype, sudo, report Markdown, and speculative-feature regressions.
Make the smallest surgical change required by the current phase.
Try to prove the change wrong by checking diff, symbols, tests, plan alignment, and project invariants.
Accept completion only when command results and final objective comparison prove it.
Maintain context.jsonl so resume after interruption continues from the exact incomplete point.

content.rule: The agent must execute these layers sequentially for every phase. Do not merge them into a vague summary.
Before editing, deeply analyze the whole project.
content.hard_stop: If these records do not exist in context.jsonl, do not edit source files.

content.when_to_use: Use this only when the prompt is incomplete but the general project direction is clear.
content.default_choice: Choose the hardest correctness-preserving FASM-first path that advances SnapSurf toward a fast, real systems language compiler.
priority_order: 3. Improve correctness and diagnostics before performance.
4. Improve performance only with baseline and measurable gate.
5. Prefer small audited FASM modules over broad mechanical conversions.
6. Prefer explicit low-level data structures over speculative high-level abstractions.
7. Add tests before or alongside behavior changes.
8. If unsure between features, choose the one closest to compiler correctness and active FASM path.
forbidden_fallbacks: Do not add unrelated language features.
Do not create a new compiler stack.
Do not move active root build to Rust, C, Python, Node, or NASM.
Do not replace the task with documentation-only work.
Do not perform shallow cleanup and call it complete.
content.required_record: Write fallback_decision to context.jsonl with reason and rejected alternatives.

example.bad_fallback: Create a general roadmap Markdown file.
example.good_fallback: Add a missing compile-fail test and implement the smallest FASM semantic check needed to pass it while preserving full regression.

content.rule: Do not create Markdown report files for status, analysis, planning, architecture, or verification.
allowed_outputs: source code changes directly required by the task
test files directly required by the task
generated code artifacts explicitly required by the build
forbidden_outputs: new documentation files unless the user explicitly requests documentation
content.note: Existing docs may be read. New report-style Markdown is forbidden.

forbidden: Do not make active root build call NASM.
Do not switch generated program assembly to NASM syntax.
Do not make Cargo/Rust prototype part of active root build.
Do not use compiler/asm as active implementation.
Do not add Python/Node/GCC/Clang/Zig/Go/NASM as active root compiler build requirements.
Do not use smoke/check-discovery as final proof.
Do not accept broad mechanical conversion without per-routine audit.

content.name: Detailed Operating Procedure: 5 Steps
content.purpose: Force Codex to execute long SnapSurf tasks as a controlled state machine instead of shallow short-session coding.
global_rules: Use context.jsonl as the single execution state file.
Do not create Markdown report files.
Do not run sudo or ask for sudo password.
Do not call partial work complete.
Continue phase by phase until final objective is complete or a real blocker is recorded.
Every step must append a structured record to context.jsonl.

step_1.name: Receive Objective and Lock the Spec
step_1.objective: Understand the user objective before touching code.
required_actions: Record original_user_objective in context.jsonl.
Extract explicit requirements, implicit requirements, forbidden actions, and success criteria.
State assumptions.
State ambiguities.
If spec is incomplete but direction is clear, apply incomplete_spec_hardcore_default.
If ambiguity can cause destructive or wrong implementation, stop and ask.
Define final_done_condition.
must_not_do: Do not simplify the user objective into a vague complete project task.
step_1.exit_gate: Step 1 passes only when final_done_condition is concrete and verifiable.

step_2.name: Analyze the Whole Project and Map Repository Reality
step_2.objective: Prevent hallucination by grounding the agent in repository reality.
required_actions: Run repository inventory using safe non-sudo commands.
Read README.md, memory/*.md, CMakeLists.txt, tests/run_all.sh.
Read compiler/fasm/main.asm include graph.
Read compiler/fasm/inc/*.inc before dependent assembly modules.
Read lexer/parser/semantic/capability/emitter/optimizer modules relevant to the task.
Read docs/tokens.md, docs/ast.md, docs/semantic_rules.md, docs/error_codes.md, docs/foundation.md.
Read tests, examples, and samples.
Read compiler/asm and prototypes/rust_stage0 only as reference material when needed.
Write architecture_map, compiler_pipeline_map, active_build_path_map, test_matrix, risk_register.
must_not_do: Do not patch after a single grep.
Do not trust old NASM wording over current FASM/CMake reality.
Do not create Markdown analysis reports.
step_2.exit_gate: Step 2 passes only when the agent can name active path, reference-only paths, relevant tests, and risky invariants.

step_3.name: Plan Phases and File Edits
step_3.objective: Break long work into phases without shrinking the objective.
required_actions: Create phase_plan with phase_id, objective, files_to_read, files_to_edit, success_criteria, verification_gate.
Create edit_plan that maps every planned file change to the original requirement.
Order phases so correctness and regression safety come before performance work.
For incomplete spec, choose the hardest correctness-preserving FASM-first path.
Predefine resume behavior for interrupted runs.
Predefine blocker criteria.
must_not_do: Do not plan documentation-only work unless explicitly requested.
Do not split into vague phases like improve compiler.
Do not use phase boundaries as a reason to stop early.
step_3.exit_gate: Step 3 passes only when each phase has concrete file scope and verification gate.

step_4.name: Execute One File at a Time with Four Mandatory Passes
step_4.objective: Make surgical code changes while preventing drift during long execution.
required_actions: Before editing a file, append file_edit_start to context.jsonl.
Re-read target file and relevant callers, callees, and includes.
Apply the smallest code change that satisfies the current phase.
After finishing one file, run all four mandatory passes.
Do not edit another source file until all four passes are passed and recorded.
step_4.exit_gate: Step 4 passes only when every edited file has four passed records.

step_5.name: Final Audit, Full Regression, and Non-Hallucinated Conclusion
step_5.objective: Prove the work is complete against the original objective.
required_actions: Run relevant narrow gate.
Run build gate.
Run hello gate if compiler/codegen behavior changed.
Run final full-regression gate.
Run binary origin check when active compiler path changed.
Re-read original_user_objective and final_done_condition.
Compare implemented result against final_done_condition.
Write final_status to context.jsonl with passed gates and remaining limitations.
must_not_do: Do not call smoke-only verification complete.
Do not say complete if full-regression was skipped without explicit reason.
Do not claim SnapSurf is self-hosting or foundation-complete.
step_5.exit_gate: Step 5 passes only when final_status is backed by command results or a real blocker.

content.problem: Codex may split long tasks into many parts due to long-running design, quota continuation, and compute management.
content.rule: Phases are allowed only as a controlled execution state machine. They must not reduce scope.
phase_requirements: Every phase must have phase_id, objective, input_state, planned_files, success_criteria, verification_gate.
Every phase must begin by reading context.jsonl and original_user_objective.
Every phase must end by writing phase_result to context.jsonl.
If interrupted, resume from the last incomplete phase in context.jsonl.
Do not ask the user to continue merely because a phase ended.
Continue automatically to the next phase until the full objective is complete or a real blocker occurs.
Do not call partial completion final.
forbidden_phase_behavior: Do not shrink the objective when splitting phases.
Do not replace implementation with planning only.
Do not stop after easy files.
Do not say complete unless final_gate passed or blocker is recorded.

content.rule: After finishing code changes in one file, verify that file four times. All four passes must pass before editing another source file.

pass_1.name: PASS_1_RE_READ_AND_DIFF
checks: Re-read the full edited file from disk.
Inspect git diff for only that file.
Confirm every changed line traces to the user request or required compile/test fix.
Confirm no unrelated formatting/refactor was introduced.
pass_1.example: After editing compiler/fasm/parser_expr.asm, read the full file and inspect git diff -- compiler/fasm/parser_expr.asm.

pass_2.name: PASS_2_PROJECT_CROSS_CHECK
checks: Check active FASM/CMake path still coherent.
Check no reference-only path became active accidentally.
pass_2.example: If parse_binary_expr changed, run rg -n "parse_binary_expr|call parse_binary_expr" . and inspect dependent modules.

pass_3.name: PASS_3_PLAN_ALIGNMENT
checks: Compare change against edit_plan in context.jsonl.
Confirm no speculative feature was added.
Confirm direction remains FASM-first, fast, correct, and systems-language oriented.
If plan changed, write plan_update to context.jsonl before continuing.
pass_3.example: If the phase objective is diagnostics correctness, do not add optimizer code.

pass_4.name: PASS_4_LOCAL_VERIFICATION
checks: Run nearest relevant command/test for changed file.
For FASM routines audit registers, stack, syscalls, signedness, and memory capacity.
Record command, exit code, and result.
pass_4.example: After semantic code changes, run a targeted compile-fail test if available, then full-regression.

content.hard_stop: If any pass fails, do not edit another file. Fix failure or record blocker.

content.resume_rule: On resume, read context.jsonl first, locate the last non-passed phase or file pass, and continue from there.
content.example: If context.jsonl ends at file_edit_end without per_file_pass_4, resume at PASS_4_LOCAL_VERIFICATION.

preapproved_non_sudo_commands: fasm commands inside project build/test context
python3 scripts that only generate local JSONL/context artifacts
content.if_blocked_by_missing_tool: Record blocker and exact missing command in context.jsonl. Ask the user to install it. Do not request password.

5. Identify whether issue is code bug, plan bug, test expectation bug, or spec ambiguity.
9. Re-run per-file four-pass if file changed.

forbidden: Do not keep layering fixes without identifying root cause.

performance_gate: If performance-sensitive code changes, collect baseline before and after.

content.rule: Completion must be proven by artifacts and commands, not prose.
required_evidence: context.jsonl contains original objective and final objective comparison.
Every edited file has four passed per-file records.
Relevant narrow gate has command, exit code, and meaning recorded.

git diff is inspected and summarized by changed file.

Do not choose low-value shallow work.

content.text:
Read this flat JSONL first. Treat it as the SnapSurf long-run anti-hallucination skill.

Important truth: you are not AGI and must not claim AGI. Your target is AGI-like engineering rigor: persistent state, whole-repository grounding, adversarial self-review, proof-of-work completion, and strict recovery from mistakes.

Use English technical terms exactly as defined in the glossary. If a term is unclear, read terminology_glossary_with_examples before acting.

Use context.jsonl as the only execution state. Do not create Markdown report files. Do not run sudo. Do not ask for passwords. Safe non-sudo repository inspection/build/test commands are preapproved.

Objective handling:
1. Record original_user_objective exactly.
2. Extract explicit requirements, implicit requirements, forbidden actions, assumptions, ambiguities, and final_done_condition.
3. If the prompt lacks complete spec but direction is clear, choose the hardest correctness-preserving FASM-first path that advances SnapSurf as a fast and correct systems language compiler.
4. Record fallback_decision and rejected alternatives if fallback is used.

Mandatory 5-step procedure:
Step 1: Receive Objective and Lock the Spec.
Step 2: Analyze the Whole Project and Map Repository Reality.
Step 3: Plan Phases and File Edits.
Step 4: Execute One File at a Time with Four Mandatory Passes.
Step 5: Final Audit, Full Regression, and Non-Hallucinated Conclusion.

After each edited file, all four checks must pass and be recorded before editing another source file:
PASS_1_RE_READ_AND_DIFF.
PASS_2_PROJECT_CROSS_CHECK.
PASS_3_PLAN_ALIGNMENT.
PASS_4_LOCAL_VERIFICATION.

Long-run rule:
Phases are allowed only as execution chunks. They must never shrink the scope. Continue automatically to the next phase until final_done_condition is satisfied or a real blocker is recorded. If interrupted or resumed, read context.jsonl first and continue from the last incomplete phase or failed pass.

SnapSurf invariants:
- Active root path is CMake + FASM.
- Active compiler source is compiler/fasm/main.asm.
- build/surf is produced by FASM.
- compiler/asm and prototypes/rust_stage0 are reference-only.
- Do not reintroduce root Makefile, active NASM, Rust prototype, Cargo, report Markdown, or speculative feature work.
- Do not claim self-hosting or foundation completion.

Failure handling:
If any check fails, stop editing, record failure, identify root cause, fix the smallest cause, rerun failed check, rerun broader gate, and repeat four-pass verification for changed files. Completion is not prose. Completion requires recorded evidence.

Context persistence rule:
The repository root must contain context.jsonl. If it does not exist, create it before source edits. Before every append, perform a context availability check: confirm that the original objective, active phase, current file or command, last result, and next action are known. If context is insufficient, do not invent records. Re-read context.jsonl, inspect git status/diff, re-read relevant files, then append context_recovered or context_insufficient_blocker. context.jsonl must record what is being done, why it is being done, verification results, blockers, and the exact resume point.

content.purpose: Create a local flat JSONL corpus for fast future reading after cloning the repository.

content.reason: Local task history can be lost after OS reinstall or home directory replacement.

content.rule: The repository must contain a project-local context.jsonl file created by the user or by the agent when allowed. The agent must use this file as the durable execution memory for the entire task.
purpose: Persist what has already been read.
Persist what is currently being done.
Persist why each file is edited.
Persist blockers, uncertainty, and resume points.
Prevent long-run hallucination and spec drift.
if_file_exists: Read the full existing context.jsonl first.
Resume from the last incomplete phase, file pass, or blocker.
Append new records only; do not rewrite history unless the user explicitly asks.
if_file_missing: Create context.jsonl at repository root before source edits.
Then continue with the required 5-step procedure.
content.hard_stop: Do not edit source files until context.jsonl exists and contains the required objective/spec records.
forbidden: Do not store secrets in context.jsonl.
Do not store sudo passwords, API keys, tokens, or private credentials.
Do not use Markdown reports as a substitute for context.jsonl.
Do not keep important task state only in chat memory.

content.rule: Before writing any context.jsonl record, the agent must check whether it still has enough reliable context to write a correct record.
content.definition: Enough context means the agent has current knowledge of the original objective, active phase, current file, last command result, and next required action.
required_check_before_each_append: Do I know the active phase_id?
Do I know the current file being edited or verified?
Do I know the exact command output or file diff I am about to record?
Do I know whether the last pass/gate passed or failed?
Do I know the next action?
Is this record based on repository facts, command output, or explicit user instruction rather than memory guess?
if_context_is_sufficient: Include evidence fields such as command, exit_code, file_path, diff_summary, or source_files_read when applicable.
if_context_is_not_sufficient: Re-read the relevant file or rerun the relevant non-destructive command.
Append context_recovered if context was restored.
Append context_insufficient_blocker if context cannot be restored safely.

example_good_record.meaning: full regression passed after emitter_fasm.asm change

example_bad_record.problem: Invalid because it does not include command, exit_code, or evidence.

content.rule: context.jsonl must record everything important the agent is doing, but in compact structured JSONL records.

content.compactness_rule: Do not dump huge file contents into context.jsonl. Store paths, symbols, command summaries, and decisions. Use the repository files as source of truth.
content.append_only_rule: Append records. If a previous record is wrong, append a correction record instead of silently editing history.
